newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli industrialists warn of 10 pct unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Israeli industrialists warn of 10 pct unemployment.

text.p: Israeli industrialists warned on Wednesday that unemployment would hit 10 percent next year if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government failed to take measures to heal the economy.
Israel's Manufacturers Association, presenting its annual economic forecast, also said exports could decline sharply as a result of the drop in investment in industry.
"We are moving towards an unemployment level of eight percent this year and if the necessary steps are not taken it could reach 10 percent next year," said the association's president Dan Propper.

Unemployment reached seven percent in the fourth quarter of last year, the last period for which figures are available, after declining steadily since 1992. Analysts say the jobless rate continued to rise in the first quarter of this year.
Propper said the government should adopt tax reforms to encourage investment in production and a reiterated his call for the Bank of Israel to lower interests rates.
"We are witnessing a dangerous slowdown in investment in industry," he told reporters in Tel Aviv.
"If this trend is not stemmed, no one should be surprised if it leads to a very sharp decline in exports in the next two to three years, especially in the high tech."
Propper lashed out at Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel for refusing to lower interest rates, describing his sole authority in setting the base interest rate as a "dictatorship".
He criticised Netanyahu for not reining in the governor.
"We regret that the prime minister is not taking the bull by the horns and leading the way to a proper economy," Proper said.
Frenkel says a tight monetary policy is necessary to keep inflation down.
